question_text: According to the course material, co-ordinating is always said to be:
explanation: Co-ordinating is always said to be the essence of management: linking activities to bring harmony and unify the process in one direction.

question_text: According to the course material, co-ordinating is the process which concerns the relationships between tasks or activities which must fit in both form and time into:
option_a: an integrated accomplishment of a goal
explanation: Co-ordinating concerns relationships between tasks that must fit in form and time into an integrated accomplishment of a goal.

question_text: According to the course material, the two essential elements of co-ordination are the tasks that must be performed and:
option_a: the timing of the task through communication
option_b: the colour of the office paint
explanation: Tasks and timing constitute the major elements; co-ordination is facilitated by communication.

question_text: According to the course material, there are basically two main types of co-ordination:
explanation: The two main types are voluntary co-ordination and directed co-ordination.

question_text: According to the course material, voluntary co-ordination is when an individual or group sees a need, finds and performs a task as necessary; to do each task well each person must have some knowledge of the goal and:
option_d: wait for a court order every minute
explanation: In voluntary co-ordination each person must know the goal and understand his position, as in the block-making example.

question_text: According to the course material, directed co-ordination is when the individual or group:
option_a: receives directive as to what to do and when to do it
explanation: Directed co-ordination is when people receive directives on what to do and when; as one finishes, the supervisor tells the next to pick it up.

question_text: According to the course material, after planning and organizing, controlling takes place; it is the process that measures current performance and guides it toward:
explanation: Controlling measures current performance and guides it toward accomplishment of some objective.

question_text: According to the course material, the two major parts of control are measuring performance against the plan and:
explanation: The two major parts of control are measuring performance against the plan and taking corrective action when needed.

question_text: According to the course material, the clearer, more complete and more packaged the plans are:
option_d: the more plans should be hidden
explanation: Controlling requires plans; clearer, more complete, more packaged plans make controls more effective.

question_text: According to the course material, measuring is the reverse of planning: the plans which come out of planning become:
option_a: the standards by which desired results are measured
explanation: Plans become the standards by which desired results are measured. Measuring also demands an organization structure so you know who takes action when results differ from the plan.

question_text: According to the course material, control should be tailored to plans, which means that control should:
explanation: Control should be tailored to plans: it should focus on result.

question_text: According to the course material, control should be economically realistic, meaning that the cost of implementing the control system must be:
option_a: less than the benefits derived from the system
explanation: Economically realistic control costs less than the benefits derived from the system.

question_text: According to the course material, control should report deviation quickly, be flexible because of changes, indicate and lead to corrective action, be simple but difficult to manipulate, and:
option_a: be acceptable to all members of the organization
explanation: Requirements include quick reporting of deviation, flexibility, leading to corrective action, simplicity that is hard to manipulate, and acceptability to all members.

question_text: According to the course material, a sign that controls are inadequate is late correction, when problems or shortfalls are discovered too late with the result that to correct them is:
explanation: Late correction means problems are discovered too late; correcting them is medicine after death.

question_text: According to the course material, other signs of inadequate control include taking unnecessary corrective action, frequent excuses by subordinates, focusing too much time on control instead of results, trying to circulate/bypass control, and:
explanation: Signs include unnecessary corrections, frequent excuses, over-focus on control rather than results, efforts to circumvent control, and a manager always checking subordinates' work.

question_text: According to the course material, directing and leading is the last management function considered in this course, and the functions are not separate and airtight; they:
option_a: are connected with one another and work as a system
explanation: Management functions are connected and work as a system; if any one is not properly applied the whole process suffers.

question_text: According to the course material, communication is the means by which people are linked together in an organization, and it makes it possible for the manager to lead and to:
option_a: control performance so that already-set objectives can be attained
explanation: Communication links people, enables change, organizes human effort, and lets the manager lead and control performance toward objectives.

question_text: According to the course material, ingredients of leadership include that leaders look at the future and create mental pictures, instill values, use power effectively, know that human beings have different needs, are a source of inspiration, and:
option_a: act in a manner that will develop a following
option_b: hide every picture of the future
explanation: Leaders create a picture of the future, instill values, use power well, recognise different needs, inspire others, and develop a following.

question_text: According to the course material, qualities of a good leader include energy, emotional stability, knowledge of human relations, empathy, personal motivation, communication skill, teaching ability, social skill and:
option_a: technical skill which provides an effective knowledge of the work
explanation: A leader must possess energy, emotional stability, human-relations knowledge, empathy, personal motivation, communication, teaching, social and technical skill.

question_text: According to the course material, empathy as a leadership quality means the leader has to:
option_a: put himself in the position of the other person
explanation: Empathy requires the leader to put himself in the position of the other person.

question_text: According to the course material, techniques of human relations include friendliness and approval, consistency and fairness, support of subordinates, use of participation, closeness of supervision once assignment is defined, settlement of grievances, and:
explanation: Human-relations techniques include friendliness, consistency and fairness, support, participation, appropriate supervision, settlement of grievances, and two-way communication.

question_text: According to the course material, inconsistent behaviour by a leader is treated under the technique of:
explanation: Inconsistent behaviour by a leader is addressed under consistency and fairness.

question_text: According to the course material, the present course is BUS 105 (also referred to in the guide as CMP 105), and further principles of management will be discussed in the second course which is:
option_a: CPM 106 / BUS 106 in the next semester
option_d: a law course in the Faculty of Law
explanation: The guide says further principles will be discussed in CPM 106 / BUS 106 next semester, with deeper coverage of some principles already introduced.

question_text: According to the course material, unnecessary activities should be identified and thrown away in co-ordinating because they constitute:
explanation: Only major or relevant activities should be identified; unnecessary activities drain organizational resources and should be thrown away.

question_text: According to the course material, the block-moulding example shows one activity linked to another through interaction, and this is brought about through:
explanation: In the block-making example, mixing, carrying, moulding, drying and stacking are linked through interaction brought about by communication.
